fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Trim back dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear width for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back any branches or shrubs that hang over or into the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency vehicles can reach the residence without obstruction.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked and mark it clearly so responders can locate and open it quickly.
• Thin dense vegetation at the rear of the property to create a path wide enough for responders on foot to reach the back of the structure.
• Mark any foot path leading from the front to the rear of the property so responders can navigate quickly without searching for a route.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Along Driveway
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Trim branches from scattered trees that hang over or touch the roofline or walls.
• Clear low-hanging branches along the driveway so vehicles and emergency responders can pass through without obstruction.
• Thin shrubs and vegetation growing along the sides of the driveway to keep the travel lane open and visible.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from mixed vegetation areas that are close to the structure.
• Keep the area behind the structure clear of shrub growth to allow movement around all sides of the building.
• Separate any shrubs or small plants growing beneath trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from ground level into the tree canopy.
• Keep the open green space areas mowed or grazed short to reduce the amount of dry grass that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so emergency vehicles can locate and use the single access route without delay.
